messages.author: 2b2a7dccb793ae6c
messages.subject: permuted
parts:
Dear Stan Users,
I am currently using the script "alpha = fit.extract(permuted=True)['alpha']" to extract the posterior samples.
But I have 4 chains and I want to preserve the full information of each chain separately without shuffling the samples.
Do I just write "alpha = fit.extract()['alpha']" and then the first quarter of alpha belongs to the first chain, etc?

Thanks!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: permuted
parts:
On Wednesday, July 13, 2016 at 12:39:57 PM UTC-4, Jingjing Chen wrote:
Dear Stan Users,
I am currently using the script "alpha = fit.extract(permuted=True)['alpha']" to extract the posterior samples.
But I have 4 chains and I want to preserve the full information of each chain separately without shuffling the samples.
Do I just write "alpha = fit.extract()['alpha']" and then the first quarter of alpha belongs to the first chain, etc?

In the extract() function, permuted = TRUE is the default, so you would have to explicitly specify permuted = FALSE. And in that case, it will output an array that is simulations by chains by number of parameters specified in the pars argument to extract. So, you would just look at the appropriate column. All of this is documented in help(extract).

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: permuted
parts:
On Saturday, July 16, 2016 at 1:26:35 AM UTC-4, Jingjing Chen wrote:
I am just a little confused. Because for example if I have parameters (alpha, beta), and when I extract them using permuted, the covariance will be lost, right?

It only permutes the rows, which are the MCMC iterations, so the covariance remains between parameters, which are the third dimension of the array.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] permuted
parts:
Yes.  You loose the autocorrelation and crosscorrelations of the _chains_,
but not the marginal covariances of the parameters themselves, which
is all you really care about.

I just want to make sure, so when I do 

a = fit.extract()['alpha']
b = fit.extract()['beta']

and plot(a,b), the covariance will be correct?
